title: Dual pushforward evaluation and projection identities
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-admissibility], with $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and write $K'=Rf_*K$. Let $D_XK$, $D_YK'$, $e_X:D_XK\otimes K\to\omega_X$, $\chi_f:Rf_*D_XK\to D_YK'$, and $\mu_{f,M,K}:Rf_*M\otimes K'\to Rf_*(M\otimes K)$ be the maps defined in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Then
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K'}\circ(\chi_f\otimes1_{K'})=\tau_f\circ Rf_*e_X\circ\mu_{f,D_XK,K},$$
and, for every such $M$,
$$\mu_{f,M,K}=Rf_*(1_M\otimes\varepsilon_f)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,K'}.$$

source.place: Step 3, proof of (a): “the defining evaluation of chi_f turns the evaluation ... into tau_f Rf_* ev_K mu_f”, and multiplication/projection identification expanded in returned item step 9

proof.text:
Put $Z=Rf_*D_XK$ and $B=\tau_f\circ Rf_*e_X\circ\mu_{f,D_XK,K}:Z\otimes K'\to\omega_Y$. By [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], $\chi_f$ is precisely the tensor–Hom transpose of $B$. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $\operatorname{ev}_{K'}$ is the inverse transpose of the identity of $R\mathcal Hom(K',\omega_Y)$. Apply the cancellation and evaluation formulas of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] in this second-variable convention to obtain
$$B=\operatorname{uncurry}(\operatorname{curry}(B))=\operatorname{ev}_{K'}\circ(\chi_f\otimes1_{K'}).$$
Explicitly, that leaf writes the fixed argument first: precompose $B$ with the signed symmetry $K'\otimes Z\to Z\otimes K'$, curry, and uncurry. Its evaluation formula gives $\operatorname{ev}^{\ell}_{K'}(1_{K'}\otimes\chi_f)$; precomposing back with the symmetry gives $\operatorname{ev}_{K'}(\chi_f\otimes1_{K'})$ by naturality of the symmetry. The two inverse symmetries cancel. This is exactly the evaluation convention specified in the two definitions, and proves the first identity.

source.place: Step 3, proof of (a): the defining evaluation of chi_f

proof.text:
For the second identity fix $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and abbreviate $L=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $T=RM\otimes RK$, with ordinary unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ from [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). Write $c:L(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}LRM\otimes LRK$ for the tensor comparison used in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], namely $\mu_{f;RM,RK}$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; at the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$ that statement identifies it with the canonical tensor comparison of the morphism of ringed pro-etale topoi induced by $f$, which is the comparison $\mu_{u;F,G}$ entering $a_{u,M,N}$ in [def-exchange-projection] for $u=f$. Set
$$a=(\varepsilon_M\otimes1_{LRK})\circ c:L(T)\to M\otimes LRK.$$
The projection-transformation definition in [def-exchange-projection], with $u=f$ and $N=RK=K'$, gives the ordinary direct-image projection map $\pi=R(a)\circ\eta_T$. This is the specified $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,K'}$: since $f$ is proper, compute its compact-support definition with the compactification $j=\operatorname{id}_X$, $p=f$. The open tensor comparison is then the identity under the unit identifications, so the defining composite is $\pi$. The compactification compatibility and proper identification in [fix-prop-projection-formula] identify this component with the stated projection map, independently of the chosen compactification. The finite-Tor input $K'$ and the finite-stage domains are exactly those stipulated by [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps].

source.place: Step 3, proof of (a): counit normalization of the projection transformation

proof.text:
Set $b=1_M\otimes\varepsilon_K:M\otimes LRK\to M\otimes K$. Tensor functoriality gives
$$b\circ a=(\varepsilon_M\otimes\varepsilon_K)\circ c.$$
By the ordinary adjunction formula $\Psi(v)=R(v)\circ\eta_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], the definition of multiplication in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] is
$$\mu_{f,M,K}=R\bigl((\varepsilon_M\otimes\varepsilon_K)\circ c\bigr)\circ\eta_T.$$
Substitute the equality for $b\circ a$ and the projection component computed in step 2. The functor composition law gives
$$\mu_{f,M,K}=R(b\circ a)\circ\eta_T=R(b)\circ R(a)\circ\eta_T=Rf_*(1_M\otimes\varepsilon_f)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,K'}.$$
Every map has source $Rf_*M\otimes K'$ and target $Rf_*(M\otimes K)$. This proves the second identity for the arbitrary $M$ chosen in step 2.
